Q: NullPointerException: Attempt to invoke virtual method 'android.app.FragmentTransaction android.app.FragmentManager.beginTransaction()' A:

This is a common Android issue. The getFragmentManager() returns null because the DialogFragment is not attached to an Activity when you try to dismiss it. This happens when:

  1. The Activity has been destroyed (user pressed back, rotated screen, etc.)

  2. The DialogFragment was never shown but dismiss() is called

  3. The fragment is already detached

Solution

Check if the fragment is added before dismissing:

public void dismissDialog() {

if (mDialogFragment != null && mDialogFragment.isAdded()) {

mDialogFragment.dismissAllowingStateLoss();

}

}

Or use a more robust check:

public void dismissDialog() {

if (mDialogFragment != null

&& mDialogFragment.getFragmentManager() != null

&& mDialogFragment.isAdded()

&& !mDialogFragment.isRemoving()) {

mDialogFragment.dismissAllowingStateLoss();

}

}

For BroadcastReceiver Scenario

Since your crash happens in a BroadcastReceiver, the Activity might be destroyed by the time the broadcast is received. Add an Activity lifecycle check:

@Override

public void onReceive(Context context, Intent intent) {

if (!isFinishing() && !isDestroyed()) {

dismissDialog();

}

}

Better Pattern: Override in DialogFragment

Create a safe dismiss method in your SimpleBlockedDialogFragment:

public class SimpleBlockedDialogFragment extends DialogFragment {

public void dismissSafe() {

if (getActivity() != null && isAdded() && !isStateSaved()) {

dismissAllowingStateLoss();

}

}

// For support library, also check:

public void dismissSafely() {

try {

if (getFragmentManager() != null) {

dismissAllowingStateLoss();

}

} catch (Exception e) {

// Already dismissed or not attached

}

}

}

Why This Happens

When you create the fragment with newInstance(), it's not attached to any Activity yet. It only gets attached when you call show(). If you call dismiss() before show(), or after the Activity is destroyed, getFragmentManager() returns null.

Your line:

private SimpleBlockedDialogFragment mDialogFragment = SimpleBlockedDialogFragment.newInstance();

This creates the object (so it's not null), but the fragment isn't attached to an Activity until show() is called.

Recommended Fix for Your Code

// In your BroadcastReceiver's updateStatus method:

public void updateStatus() {

if (mDialogFragment != null

&& mDialogFragment.isAdded()

&& !isFinishing()) {

mDialogFragment.dismissAllowingStateLoss();

}

}

Q: How to install local packages using pip as part of a docker build? A:

First of all, you need to add other_module to your Docker image. Without that, the pip install command will not be able to find it. However you can not ADD a directory that is outside the directory of the Dockerfile according to the documentation:

The <src> path must be inside the context of the build; you cannot ADD ../something /something, because the first step of a docker build is to send the context directory (and subdirectories) to the docker daemon.

So you have to move the other_module directory into the same directory as your Dockerfile, i.e. your structure should look something like

.
├── Dockerfile
├── requirements.txt
├── other_module
|   ├── modue_file.xyz
|   └── another_module_file.xyz

then add the following to the dockerfile:

ADD /other_module /other_module
ADD requirements.txt /app
WORKDIR /app
RUN pip install -r requirements.txt

The WORKDIR command moves you into /app so the next step, RUN pip install... will be executed inside the /app directory. And from the app-directory, you now have the directory../other_module avaliable

Q: Why is PostgreSQL COPY significantly slower than SQL Server BULK INSERT? A:

I have 30 .CSV files that are loaded into 6 different tables.

Regarding performance testing, I believe establishing a baseline is essential. The current description lacks the detail necessary for others to reproduce your results. To make this actionable, we need to clarify the following:

  • (1) Data Scale: How many records are in a single CSV file? What is the average file size (e.g., 100 MB or 1 GB)?
  • (2) A Small Sample CSV Data.
  • (3) Schema Structure: What are the Table DDLs for both the original SQL Server version and the target PostgreSQL version?
  • (4) Execution Method: How was the COPY command executed? Was it run directly via the Terminal? Please provide the exact command-line syntax used.
  • (5) Benchmarks: What were your observed execution times? 1 hour or 30 mins ?
  • (6) Operating system and version? Are SQL Server and PostgreSQL installed on Windows or Linux?

Providing these details is the only way for others to replicate the test in their own environments and verify the findings.

Q: Can't get personal access tokens to work with github for own repo A:

First, make sure your token has at least the repo scope.

Second, the GitHub official documentation confirms:

$ git clone https://github.com/username/repo.git
Username: your_username
Password: your_token

Double-check the output of git config --global credential.helper to make sure nothing was cached. The only one I use on CentOS7 is git config --global credential.helper 'cache --timeout 3600'.

Check also your version of Git (I know on my CentOS7 server, it can be... quite old: 1.8.x! And yes, no SSH egress would ever be allowed)

Finally, from this thread, try and make sure you have 2FA activated for your GitHub account.
